scope: Sequence complete-document persistence; controlled native-event unit fixtures, no browser or broad suite claim.

red.cause: Actual deliberate implementation stubs rejected all original cases.

fixtureCorrection.explanation: An added native-put fault initially replaced an objectStore method after admission had already captured its object; that case exercised success, so its first pass does not prove write-failure handling. The final fixture injects the fault in the captured put function before request callbacks and asserts protected state, unchanged old row, actual rollback, and explicit successful reload/retry. A wrong-working-directory edit attempt was a setup error and did not modify tracked files.

verified: Proven absence versus present undefined; no startup write or corrupt fallback
Exact complete archive-byte and row CAS, including semantically equivalent but reordered archive bytes
Legacy migration in memory and exact original localStorage retention; pre/inside/post-transaction fencing
Fresh third-writer-safe one-shot replacement and bounded corrupt archive recovery
Unknown and oversized opaque rows refuse blind replacement
Detached candidate publication and failed validation preserving accepted authority
Native put failure waits actual rollback and preserves old complete row
Prompt cancellation/timeout retains native slot until terminal, including late open
Already committed withheld completion retains durable row without falsely claiming rollback or authority

ui.notes: load is nonauthorizing until acceptLoad; save/replace resolve only after actual complete. Prompt rejected operations retain nativePending until drain; close awaits it. UI owns save coalescing and matching-generation Saved presentation.

limitations: Controlled unit fixture is not physical or real IndexedDB runtime evidence; independent native coverage is parent-coordinated.
No atomic transaction spans localStorage and IndexedDB; a post-complete foreign legacy change protects the already durable new row.
Unsupported raw shapes remain protected; recovery is only offered for bounded known data.
